answer: It is recorded as a censored value at the horizon, not as a completed duration. The rollback state records three things: whether the rollback completed within the horizon; the time from trigger to drain, or a censored value at the horizon; and the maximum divergence observed before the trigger. So when the modeled drain is still running at the end of the horizon, the trigger-to-drain time is neither zero nor extrapolated to a finish time — it is right-censored at the observation boundary, paired with an explicit 'did not complete within the horizon' flag. The page treats this as a legitimate finding rather than a failed model: non-completion means the declared reconciliation capacity is insufficient for the declared lag and observation window, which is exactly the conclusion a precise but meaningless duration (for example, an unknown recorded as zero) would hide.
